provenance.note: The 68 methodology questions, 10 domains, weights, critical/hard-gate flags and the 0-5 response scale are reproduced verbatim from the approved MFRS-V1.0 seed. They are NOT modified by this prototype.
provenance.prototype_additions: Gateway questions (G-*) and outsourced-oversight variants (OV-*) are PROTOTYPE PLACEHOLDERS. They are not approved production content. See docs/adaptive-assessment/11-content-decisions-required.md.

response_scale.label: Not in place
response_scale.operationalMeaning: The control, process or capability does not exist or is not recognised as required.

response_scale.label: Initial / ad hoc
response_scale.operationalMeaning: Some activity may occur informally or reactively, but it is not defined, owned or reliable.

response_scale.label: Partially designed
response_scale.operationalMeaning: Some elements exist, but implementation is incomplete, inconsistent or not evidenced.

response_scale.label: Implemented
response_scale.operationalMeaning: The capability is established in important areas, but may not operate consistently across the organisation.

response_scale.label: Consistently operating
response_scale.operationalMeaning: The capability is formally implemented, evidenced and regularly operating.

response_scale.label: Embedded and improved
response_scale.operationalMeaning: The capability is monitored, measured, governed and continuously improved.

uncertainty_option.label: I do not know
uncertainty_option.helper: Recorded as uncertainty. This is not treated as a control being absent, and it is not treated as a control being present.

domains.name: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring

gateways.prompt: Which best describes what your organisation does?
gateways.display_guidance: This helps us ask only the questions that apply to how you actually operate.
gateways.report_implication: Sets sector framing for the report narrative.

gateways.prompt: Roughly how many people work in the organisation?
gateways.display_guidance: Approximate is fine. Size changes which controls are realistic to expect.

gateways.prompt: Does your organisation buy goods or services from external suppliers or contractors?
gateways.display_guidance: Include regular suppliers, subcontractors, agencies and professional firms you pay.

response_options.label: Yes, and we manage those relationships ourselves
Yes, but supplier management is handled by an external provider
Yes, and it is handled by a group or shared service function
No, we do not use external suppliers or contractors

gateways.report_implication: Determines whether supplier fraud exposure is assessed directly or as third-party governance.

gateways.prompt: How is buying and procurement handled?
gateways.display_guidance: We ask because procurement is one of the most common places fraud occurs.

response_options.label: A dedicated procurement or buying function
Owners or managers buy directly, with no formal department
An external provider does it for us
A group or shared service function does it

gateways.report_implication: Switches procurement questions between direct control and oversight framing.

gateways.prompt: Does your organisation handle physical cash?
gateways.display_guidance: Cash includes till floats, petty cash and cash takings.

response_options.label: Yes, regularly and in meaningful amounts

gateways.prompt: Does your organisation hold physical stock, inventory or valuable equipment?
gateways.display_guidance: Include goods for sale, raw materials, tools and site plant.
Payroll fraud is common, but the control questions differ depending on who runs it.

response_options.label: An external payroll provider runs it
A group or shared service function runs it
We have no payroll (for example, owner-only)

gateways.report_implication: Switches payroll integrity between direct control and provider oversight.

gateways.prompt: Do you sell online or accept digital or card payments?
gateways.display_guidance: Include card machines, online checkout, EFT and payment links.

response_options.label: Yes, but only through a third-party platform or marketplace

gateways.report_implication: Determines digital fraud domain applicability and framing.

gateways.prompt: Do you hold personal information about customers, clients or employees?
gateways.display_guidance: Names with contact details, ID numbers, or banking details all count.
gateways.report_implication: Drives identity and data exposure weighting.

gateways.prompt: Do you process refunds, credit notes or manual adjustments?
gateways.display_guidance: These are frequent routes for internal fraud, so we ask about them directly.

gateways.prompt: Does the organisation operate from more than one site, store or project location?
gateways.display_guidance: Dispersed operations make oversight harder, so we adjust the questions.

gateways.prompt: Do you use temporary, seasonal or subcontracted workers?
gateways.display_guidance: Short-tenure workers change how access and oversight need to work.
gateways.report_implication: Drives workforce-transience exposure and access-control emphasis.

gateways.prompt: Do employees work remotely, or do you depend on third-party digital platforms to operate?
gateways.display_guidance: Examples include cloud accounting, hosted systems and remote access to company systems.

gateways.prompt: Who approves payments and significant spending?
gateways.display_guidance: There is no wrong answer. Owner-led approval is common and we assess it on its own terms.

response_options.label: A formal delegation of authority with defined limits
The owner or a single director approves everything
A group or shared service function approves

gateways.report_implication: Calibrates segregation-of-duties expectations for small organisations.

questions.prompt: A senior executive or leadership function has clear accountability for fraud risk management.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether fraud risk has named leadership ownership.
questions.evidence_prompt: Board pack, role profile or delegation of authority naming the fraud risk owner.

questions.prompt: Fraud risk is formally recognised within the organisation's enterprise risk management framework.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether fraud is integrated into the wider risk framework.
questions.evidence_prompt: Risk register or ERM framework showing fraud as a named risk.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks and incidents are periodically reported to senior leadership or governance committees.
questions.display_guidance: Tests leadership visibility and reporting rhythm.
questions.evidence_prompt: Minutes or a standing agenda item covering fraud.

questions.prompt: Responsibility for fraud risk management is clearly distinguished from internal audit's independent assurance role.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether management ownership is confused with assurance.
questions.evidence_prompt: Terms of reference distinguishing management and assurance duties.

questions.prompt: The organisation has defined policies or guidance that outline how fraud risks should be prevented, detected and managed.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether there is formal guidance for fraud risk management.
questions.evidence_prompt: Fraud policy, code of conduct or equivalent guidance.

questions.prompt: Leadership is informed about emerging fraud risks affecting the organisation's sector or operating environment.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether leadership sees fraud as dynamic and external-facing.
questions.evidence_prompt: Briefings, sector alerts or advisory updates shared with leadership.

questions.prompt: The organisation has conducted a structured fraud risk assessment within the past two years.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether fraud risk has been deliberately assessed.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks have been mapped across key operational processes such as procurement, payments, refunds, claims and supplier management.
questions.evidence_prompt: Process-level fraud risk map or matrix.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks are considered when introducing new products, services or digital platforms.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether change introduces fraud review.
questions.evidence_prompt: Change or product approval checklist including fraud review.

questions.prompt: The organisation periodically reviews fraud risks in response to operational changes or new market developments.
questions.display_guidance: Tests whether fraud-risk identification is refreshed.
questions.evidence_prompt: Review cadence or refreshed risk register versions.

questions.prompt: Fraud risks related to third-party relationships, suppliers or intermediaries have been assessed.
questions.evidence_prompt: Third-party risk assessment or supplier risk register.

questions.prompt: Emerging fraud threats affecting the organisation's industry or sector are actively monitored.
questions.evidence_prompt: Threat monitoring subscriptions, alerts or briefings.

questions.prompt: The organisation considers how fraud could occur through misuse of internal authority, system access or operational processes.
questions.display_guidance: Tests insider and access-abuse risk thinking.
questions.evidence_prompt: Insider risk or access-abuse scenarios in the risk assessment.

questions.prompt: The organisation considers how fraud could occur through customer platforms, digital channels, loyalty programmes or service ecosystems.
questions.evidence_prompt: Digital channel fraud scenarios in the risk assessment.

questions.prompt: High-risk processes such as procurement, payments or refunds include segregation of duties between initiation, approval and reconciliation.
questions.evidence_prompt: Process maps or system roles showing separated duties.
questions.small_org_note: If the owner approves everything, answer on how initiation and review are separated in practice.

questions.prompt: Transactions above defined financial thresholds require independent review or approval.
questions.evidence_prompt: Delegation of authority or approval matrix.

questions.prompt: Supplier onboarding processes include background checks, verification of business information or due diligence.
questions.evidence_prompt: Supplier onboarding checklist or vetting records.

questions.prompt: System access rights are restricted based on job responsibilities and reviewed periodically.
questions.display_guidance: Tests access control and periodic review.
questions.evidence_prompt: Access review records or role matrix.

questions.prompt: Sensitive financial activities such as refunds, credits or manual adjustments are monitored or reviewed.
questions.display_guidance: Tests monitoring of high-risk manual activities.

questions.prompt: The organisation periodically reviews operational processes to identify control weaknesses or opportunities for manipulation.
questions.evidence_prompt: Process review notes or internal control testing.

questions.prompt: Individuals involved in high-risk activities are subject to oversight, rotation of duties or secondary review.
questions.display_guidance: Tests people-layer oversight in sensitive roles.
questions.evidence_prompt: Rotation schedules or secondary review evidence.

questions.prompt: The organisation monitors transactions or operational activities for unusual patterns or anomalies.
Exception reports highlighting unusual transactions or activities are generated and reviewed regularly.
Data analytics, monitoring reports or automated rules are used to identify unusual transactions, behavioural anomalies or control exceptions.
questions.evidence_prompt: Analytics rules, dashboards or alert configurations.

questions.prompt: Detection mechanisms are updated periodically to reflect new fraud risks or emerging threats.
questions.evidence_prompt: Change log for detection rules or reports.

questions.prompt: Monitoring processes cover both internal fraud risks and external fraud threats.
Individuals responsible for monitoring suspicious activity have clear authority to escalate concerns.
Internal audit or risk functions periodically review detection mechanisms to assess their effectiveness.
questions.display_guidance: Tests independent review of detection controls.
questions.evidence_prompt: Audit or assurance reports covering detection.

questions.prompt: The organisation has a documented process for responding to suspected fraud incidents.
questions.display_guidance: Tests existence of formal response framework.
questions.evidence_prompt: Fraud response plan or incident procedure.

questions.prompt: Employees understand how and where to report suspected fraud or misconduct.
There are defined roles and responsibilities for managing fraud investigations.
questions.evidence_prompt: Named investigation roles or panel terms of reference.

questions.prompt: Fraud investigations follow structured procedures that ensure fairness, confidentiality and proper documentation.
Evidence related to suspected fraud incidents is handled and preserved appropriately.
The organisation considers engaging external specialists when incidents require forensic, legal or investigative expertise.
questions.evidence_prompt: Panel arrangements or prior specialist engagements.

questions.prompt: Lessons learned from fraud incidents are used to improve controls and reduce future risk.
questions.evidence_prompt: Post-incident review notes and resulting control changes.

questions.prompt: The organisation provides a confidential or anonymous channel for reporting suspected fraud or misconduct.
questions.evidence_prompt: Hotline details or reporting channel communications.

questions.prompt: Employees are aware of how to report concerns through the whistleblowing channel.
Reports submitted through the whistleblowing channel are reviewed and investigated independently.
The organisation communicates that retaliation against whistleblowers is prohibited.
Whistleblowing channels are accessible to external stakeholders such as suppliers, contractors or customers.
Employees receive guidance or training on recognising and reporting suspicious behaviour.
questions.display_guidance: Tests practical reporting and detection awareness.

questions.prompt: Suppliers, contractors or vendors are subject to background checks or due diligence before being engaged.

questions.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
questions.prompt: Procurement processes include safeguards designed to reduce risks of collusion or manipulation.
questions.evidence_prompt: Tender rules, rotation policy or bid evaluation records.

questions.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
questions.prompt: The organisation requires employees to disclose conflicts of interest involving suppliers or third parties.

questions.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
questions.prompt: Supplier payment processes include verification mechanisms to reduce risks such as invoice manipulation or vendor impersonation.

questions.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
questions.prompt: High-risk suppliers or third-party relationships are periodically reviewed or monitored.

questions.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
questions.prompt: Procurement or vendor management activities are subject to oversight or periodic review.
questions.evidence_prompt: Procurement audit or management review records.

questions.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
questions.prompt: The organisation considers fraud risks when entering partnerships, distribution arrangements or intermediary relationships.
The organisation has processes to verify the identity of customers, users or counterparties where appropriate.
questions.evidence_prompt: Identity verification procedure or system configuration.

questions.prompt: Systems or platforms are monitored for suspicious behaviour such as unusual login activity or account access patterns.
Employees receive training on recognising phishing, social engineering and digital impersonation attempts.
Access to sensitive systems is restricted and regularly reviewed.
The organisation monitors digital activity to detect potential misuse or unauthorised transactions.
Employees and users are encouraged to report suspicious digital activity or security concerns.
The organisation periodically reviews emerging digital fraud risks relevant to its operations or sector.
The organisation has processes to detect identity misuse, account takeover or impersonation risks affecting customers or employees.
Employees receive periodic training or guidance on recognising fraud risks relevant to the organisation.
Fraud awareness is included as part of employee onboarding or induction processes.
Leadership communicates clear expectations regarding ethical conduct and fraud prevention.
questions.display_guidance: Tests leadership tone and ethics message.

questions.prompt: Employees understand the consequences of engaging in fraudulent or unethical behaviour.
The organisation communicates real examples or scenarios to help employees recognise fraud risks.
Employees feel comfortable raising concerns about suspicious behaviour without fear of negative consequences.
questions.display_guidance: Tests cultural safety and speak-up confidence.
questions.evidence_prompt: Culture survey results or speak-up metrics.

questions.section: Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring
questions.prompt: The organisation periodically reviews its fraud risks and control environment.

questions.section: Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring
questions.prompt: Fraud incidents or control failures are analysed to identify underlying causes.

questions.section: Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring
questions.prompt: Lessons learned from investigations or incidents are used to improve controls and processes.
questions.evidence_prompt: Control change log tied to incidents.

questions.section: Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring
questions.prompt: The organisation monitors fraud trends affecting its industry or operating environment.

questions.section: Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring
questions.prompt: Fraud risks are considered when implementing new systems, products or operational changes.
questions.evidence_prompt: Change control checklist with fraud step.

questions.section: Continuous Improvement and Fraud Risk Monitoring
questions.prompt: Leadership periodically evaluates whether existing fraud controls remain effective.

oversight_variants.prompt: Your organisation confirms that supplier management is handled by an external provider. The organisation obtains assurance that the provider performs supplier vetting and due diligence to an agreed standard.
oversight_variants.display_guidance: Outsourcing moves the activity, not the risk. We assess how well you govern the provider.
oversight_variants.evidence_prompt: Service agreement clauses, provider assurance reports or vetting attestations.

oversight_variants.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
oversight_variants.prompt: The organisation defines and monitors the vetting standard its external provider must apply before third parties are engaged on its behalf.
oversight_variants.display_guidance: We are assessing your oversight of the provider, not the provider's own controls.
oversight_variants.evidence_prompt: Contractual vetting standard and monitoring records.

oversight_variants.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
oversight_variants.prompt: Where procurement is performed by an external provider, the organisation retains defined controls over supplier selection, price integrity and conflict-of-interest disclosure.
oversight_variants.display_guidance: Outsourced procurement concentrates collusion risk at the provider. We assess retained control.
oversight_variants.evidence_prompt: Retained approval rights, spend analytics or independent price checks.

oversight_variants.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
oversight_variants.prompt: Where supplier payments are executed by an external provider, the organisation independently verifies changes to supplier banking details before payments are released.
oversight_variants.display_guidance: Vendor impersonation remains your loss even when a provider processes the payment.
oversight_variants.evidence_prompt: Independent callback or verification procedure covering provider-executed payments.

oversight_variants.prompt: Where sales run through a third-party platform, the organisation reviews the fraud, dispute and account-security reporting that the platform provides.
oversight_variants.display_guidance: You may not control the platform, but you can govern how you use its fraud reporting.
oversight_variants.evidence_prompt: Platform fraud or dispute reports with evidence of review.

oversight_variants.section: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
oversight_variants.prompt: Where payroll is processed by an external provider, the organisation independently reviews the payroll register for unknown, duplicate or altered employee records.
oversight_variants.display_guidance: Ghost-employee fraud survives outsourcing unless someone in your organisation reviews the register.
oversight_variants.evidence_prompt: Payroll register review records signed by someone independent of the provider.

skip_reason_codes.gateway_no_high_risk_handling: The organisation confirmed it handles no cash, stock, refunds or temporary workers.
skip_reason_codes.gateway_no_digital_footprint: The organisation confirmed it has no online sales, digital payments or platform dependency.
skip_reason_codes.gateway_no_digital_or_identity_footprint: The organisation confirmed it has no digital sales channel and holds no personal information.
skip_reason_codes.gateway_no_employee_base: The organisation confirmed it has no employees beyond the owner.
skip_reason_codes.upstream_answer_changed: A gateway answer was changed and this question is no longer on the active pathway.
skip_reason_codes.redirected_to_oversight_variant: The activity is outsourced, so the third-party governance equivalent was asked instead.

gateway_blocks.title: About your organisation
gateway_blocks.intro: First, five short questions about how your organisation operates. They decide which parts of the assessment apply to you, so we only ask what is relevant.

gateway_blocks.title: Before we assess fraud risk identification
gateway_blocks.intro: Before we assess how your organisation identifies fraud risk, we need to understand how much of your operation depends on remote working and third-party digital platforms.

gateway_blocks.title: Before we assess operational controls
gateway_blocks.intro: Before we assess your operational fraud controls, we need to understand where money, stock and people actually move through your business.

gateway_blocks.title: Before we assess supplier and procurement controls
gateway_blocks.intro: Before we assess supplier and procurement controls, we need to understand how your organisation purchases goods and services, and how payroll is run.
